observation.visible_scene: A wide beach at dusk/dawn under a sky filled with pink-and-grey altocumulus clouds and a bright orange band at the horizon. Silhouetted port cranes and a long jetty sit on the right horizon; low buildings line the left horizon. The foreground is wet sand covered by a thin, mirror-like film of seawater that reflects the orange sky and clouds. The camera viewpoint and the horizon landmarks (cranes, buildings) stay in the same pixel positions throughout the excerpt, indicating a static shot.
visible_changes: Shallow water advances and retreats over the sand: a foam-edged wave tongue pushes leftward into the reflective foreground around frames 2-3, then recedes leaving scattered foam patches in frames 3-5.
After the first backwash, the foreground settles into a smooth, foam-free reflective sheet for a long interval (roughly frames 6-15).
A second, gentler wave edge with a thin foam line re-enters from the right around frames 16-19 and withdraws by frames 20-23, again leaving brief foam streaks.
From about frame 24 to the end, the surface remains a calm reflective film with only minor shimmer, no new foam front crossing the frame.

The reflected orange sunset band and cloud pattern on the wet surface shift subtly in brightness and ripple texture as the water film thickness changes, but the sky itself and the distant silhouettes show no discernible movement.
No editing cut is visible; the changes are continuous physical motion of the water surface.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the wave cycle continues, strengthens, or calms after the last frame, and what preceded the first frame's incoming tongue.
The exact position and motion of the sun (it is below the horizon band), and any tide level change over a longer timescale.
Whether the clouds drift appreciably over a period longer than this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is treated as static because the horizon structures and frame edges remain fixed; any very slow pan/zoom is not supported by the visible evidence.
Apparent cloud 'motion' cannot be confirmed as drift versus reflection ripple, so it is not asserted.
The distinction between a thin standing water film and a very shallow swash in the long smooth intervals is not resolvable from these frames.
